text:
mike: Heads-up — we saw a ~12% interruption rate for GPU spot instances in us-west-2 around 03:15 UTC. Several inference pods stayed Pending while the autoscaler tried to reallocate. Thinking we need an "on-demand buffer" that scales up automatically when interrupts spike. Anyone seen this pattern recently?

sarah: I saw the same. Scheduler events show nodebinding delays + image pull stalls. Pods waited ~60s then bound to on-demand nodes. :grimacing:

josh: Can you paste the k8s events and node termination log snippets?

mike: pasted logs below (shortened):
```
I0315 03:15:12.234 kubelet termination: Node /i-0abcd preempted by provider (shutdown)
I0315 03:15:13.002 scheduler: Pod default/runner-abc Pending: insufficient nodes
I0315 03:16:10.892 controller: launched node group on-demand-1 (capacity 4)
```

sarah: The pattern: short burst of spot evictions -> multi-second delay to spin on-demand nodes in that AZ -> scheduler backlog. Our static "min_spot_floor" was too low.

josh: Proposed approach: keep a lightweight dynamic floor per-region that reacts to recent eviction rate. Something like: if interrupt_rate_5m > 5% then increase on-demand floor by min(20%, interrupt_rate * 2) with a cooldown of 5m.

ana: Cost concern: auto-growing on-demand by 20% across clusters could blow the monthly bill if multiple regions spike. Need caps and a decay window. Also prefer per-cluster budget boundaries.

mike: Agreed. Thoughts on heuristics: use a combination of:
- interrupt_rate (5m)
- pending_pod_count (avg 1m)
- time-to-bind median (1m)
If pending_pod_count spikes + interrupt_rate high -> bump on-demand buffer.

josh: Draft autoscaler config proto:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  mode: mixed-capacity
  static_floor: 0.05         # baseline on-demand fraction
  dynamic_buffer:
    enabled: true
    lookback: 5m
    interrupt_threshold: 0.05
    max_increase_pct: 0.20  # cap of +20% on-demand
    cooldown: 5m
    decay: 15m
  region_caps:
    us-west-2: 0.25
    us-east-1: 0.30
  burst_pool:
    enabled: true
    size: 20               # nodes in burst pool per region
    prewarm_timeout: 30s
```

sarah: +1 to region caps. Also add a per-project cost cap override so high-cost teams can opt out or get billed separately.

ana: For graceful degraded performance: before adding on-demand, we should try to drain KV cache and reduce long-tail requests by throttling heavy queries. That reduces immediate pressure and avoids overprovisioning.

josh: Good point — implement a pre-fallback step: throttle non-critical requests and enable KV prefix cache hits for active sessions. If backlog doesn't clear in 30s, escalate to bump.

mike: ops checklist idea:
- detect: interruption_rate_5m > 5% AND pending_pods > 10
- throttle: set route weight non-prod -> 0.2, slow heavy ops
- reactive: increase on-demand buffer up to max_increase_pct
- fallback: if regions unhealthy, route to alternate region (respect data residency)

ops-oncall: Adding alert: interrupt_rate_us-west-2 > 5% for 3m -> Pager. I'll open the alert PR.

infra-bot: Deploy plan created: pr/infra/autoscaler/dynamic-buffer#47 by @sarah — schedule review.

ana: We should also consider a tiny warm pool (pre-warmed on-demand instances) with a very short prewarm_timeout (20-30s). Cheaper than cold spins and reduces tail latency. Keep it small and regional.

josh: Agree. Burst pool policy: keep ephemeral on-demand instances in Stopped/Standby, then Start on demand — quicker than new instance creation. But requires instance lifecycle changes + spot allocation gating.

mike: Network constraint note — us-west-2 had transient EBS attach latencies. Spinning up on-demand is not just instance latency; block device attach + image pull matters. So warm pool should keep images cached and EBS attached snapshot warmed where possible.

ana: For the cost model, let's simulate 3 scenarios: (1) baseline static floor 5%, (2) dynamic buffer with max +10%, (3) dynamic buffer with max +20% + warm pool. We'll run 48h replay using last month's eviction traces and compute delta cost + p99 latency.

sarah: I'll coordinate the replay job. Plan to run on staging with synthetic traffic, then run one region.

josh: Action items:
- @sarah open PR with autoscaler config + unit tests (deadline end of day today)
- @mike run the 48h replay and post results by EOD tomorrow
- @ana produce cost projection table for the 3 scenarios
- @ops-oncall add Alert + runbook for sustained interrupt spikes

ops-oncall: Acked and will document runbook steps (throttle -> bump -> failover).

mike: One more: let's add an 'eviction_budget' metric exported to our billing dashboards — how much eviction headroom we tolerate before safety rollback.

ana: Yep, and ensure fleet quotas respect per-region caps so dynamic buffer doesn't eat into reserved capacity for enterprise customers.

sarah: I'll include a sample pod annotation to opt-out of dynamic buffer for sensitive workloads:
```yaml
annotations:
  inference.redwood.io/dynamic-on-demand: "false"
```

josh: Nice. If everyone is aligned I'll land a minimal config (static_floor + dynamic_buffer toggles + caps) and we can iterate after replay. :rocket:

mike: Sounds good. Thanks all. I'll follow up with the replay artifacts and a short summary slide for tomorrow's infra sync. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: Closing loop here — will page if alert fires.

mike: 👍
